entries.text: After CreateMeshPartAsync, sanity-check part.Size against the 5-stud character BEFORE judging looks: hand weapons belong at ~2.5-4 studs total; the first procedural scimitar shipped at 9.6 studs (double player height) and read as absurd.

A generated blade only reads as a blade with a converging apex point, thin cross-section (thickness well under width), and a distinct guard+pommel breaking the hilt silhouette; a thick rounded shaft with a blunt tip reads phallic.

Before judging a build of any real-world object, pull actual reference proportions first (exemplars or a web lookup) and compare feature-by-feature - judging the scimitar from memory shipped a disc guard and missed that scimitar-family hilts use cross quillons with a hooked/rounded pommel (kilij: yelman flare in the last 30% of the blade).

FIT GRIPS AT T-POSE, VERIFY AT USE-POSES: fist-up is perpendicular to the arm only when the arm is horizontal - on a hanging arm it parallels the forearm bone, embedding a straight blade ~1.5 studs INSIDE the limb while grip offset/angle still read 0/0 (measured 2026-07-10). So: reset_pose to T-pose, grip_tool frame alignment, apply the ~15-25 deg forward cant, then check blade_in_arm_studs at the REST pose and clip_self_intersect across the swing - the fitting pose passing means nothing about the poses the weapon will actually be used in.
